brief: Core PCE rose 0.25% in August, pushing the year-over-year rate to 3.01%, below expectations after a methodological revision. GS Economics (Mericle) sees an October Fed hike as unlikely, pushes the second hike to December, and sees a strong chance the FOMC skips further hikes. FX strategist Jenkins notes the market still prices October near 50-50 and flags Waller's speech today as the next signal. On France, OAT-Bund widening reflects election and energy-driven risk aversion rather than new fundamentals, since growth, deficit, budget news and polls have all stayed stable. The budget proposal targets a 5% deficit versus 5.4% previously expected, though GS expects 5.3% actual. Debt/GDP is seen rising to 125% by the next decade, and Melenchon's rise to second in first-round polls is flagged as a tail risk through his proposal to cancel French debt. GS estimates September ISM manufacturing held at 54.6 even as its own survey tracker softened to 56.1, with the services PMI seen as an outlier likely to normalize. Ahead of Brazil's October 4 election, GS favors receiving the DI curve and rate-sensitive equities. FX Sales (Wade) reports clients broadly unhedged and pitches cheap tail hedges in Brent, AUDUSD and a one-year SPX/SOFR dual binary.
